newsitem.title: FINLAND: Main events in Finland's history.
newsitem.headline: Main events in Finland's history.

text.p: Following are some key dates in Finland's history.
* 1917 October Revolution -- Finland, former Grand Duchy of Russian empire, gains independence.
* 1918 Civil War -- Bolsheviks help leftist "Reds" against establishment "whites", but Reds are defeated. German troops in Finland. Peace of Tartu, 1920, regularises Soviet border.
* 1935 -- Finland sets course as Nordic neutral state.
* August 23, 1939 -- Nazi-Soviet pact signed, secretly putting Finland inside Soviet "sphere of influence".
* November 30, 1939 Winter War -- to March 13 1940. Finland retains independence, cedes eastern territory to Soviet Union.
* June 1941: German soldiers in Finland, allied with Finland by Germany's plan to invade Soviet Union. Finland declares war on Soviet Union on June 25.

* June 26, 1941 Continuation War -- to September 5, 1944. Finns regain territory surrendered in Winter War; but German losses spark counter-attack in 1944. Finland breaks relations with Germany in September, truce with Soviet Union signed September 19.
* September 15, 1944 Lapland War -- to April 25, 1945: Finland removes remaining German troops from its territory as part of the truce.
* Autumn 1944: more than 400,000 people from eastern area of Karelia seek refuge as their homes are lost to Soviet Union.
* 1945 Russian-led Allied Control Commission resides at Hotel Torni, central Helsinki, until autumn 1947.

* April 6, 1948 -- Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance with Soviet Union signed. Finland is committed to repel "an armed attack by Germany or any allied state" against Finland or the Soviet Union through Finland. Formally renounced by both parties on January 20 1992.
* 1955 Finland joins United Nations --despite Soviet opposition
* 1961 Finland becomes associate member of European Free Trade Agreement (EFTA)
* October 30, 1961 "Note Crisis", Soviet Union requests military consultation under Treaty, just before presidential election.
* 1969 Finland begins to host SALT talks (Strategic Arms limitation Treaty), starts pressing western Europe and the United States for European Security Conference.
* 1975 Conference for Security and Cooperation in Europe (CSCE) meets in Helsinki, Helsinki Act is signed.
* 1989 Finland joins the Council of Europe
* 1994 Finland joins NATO's Partnership for Peace.
* 1995 Finland joins European Union, giving the EU a 1,300 km (800 mile) border with Russia.
